sections.heading: Chhou dance
sections.content: is performed in the Jharkhand. This dance has evolved during the course of interactions with other neighboring cultures of West Bengal and Bihar. It is a dance mostly done in open field and in the night. The dance arena is generally surrounded by fire poles .The artists go for a bath and puja before performing this dance as the characters they play are of Gods. The Chhou dancers use colourful decorative masks of big size. These masks are made of paper mache', light wood and paper. Chhou naach is a tribal form of nritya natika (dance- drama) where various characters with Chhou masks play mythological characters. Most of these plays are based on epics of Mahabharat and Ramayan which makes it very spiritual and respectful. The characters of Chhou dance wear traditions ornaments and dance with weapons. Their clothes are very colourful. This dance involves lots of gymnastic actions in the dance sequences and most of the characters are very aggressive in nature. This dance drama is supported by traditions nagada (drums) and flute as background sound and rhythm of dance action varies with the modulations of drum beats.

sections.heading: Jharkhand  Handicrafts- Masks
sections.content: Chhou is a type of dance done with colourful masks. The mask is made of papier mache in Singhbhum district of Jharkhand. These dancers use colourful, big sized and decorative masks. The masks are bright in colour and the details are stylised.

sections.heading: Jharkhand  Handicrafts- Bamboo Craft
sections.content: The forests of Jharkhand have a good quality, thin but strong and flexible bamboo. Such bamboo is used by the artisans for making different items out of the bamboo, such as fishing equipments, baskets, containers, hunting equipments and fishing gears are made.

sections.heading: Jharkhand  Handicrafts- Paitkar Paintings
sections.content: A form of painting famous from Jharkhand is a special type of painting called the paitkar paintings. This form of painting is one of the earliest forms of tribal paintings in India. These paintings have the look of a scroll on which life after death is depicted. It is unfortunate that, due to lack of recognition and promotion, this type of painting is slowly facing extinction.

sections.heading: Jharkhand  Handicrafts- Toy Making
sections.content: Toupadana near the capital city of Ranchi is famous for some unusual wooden toys that are completely abstract. They are just pieces of wood painted to look like human figures with angular lines but no separate limbs. Hands are indicated only by painting lines on the body. The toys are always in pairs showing man and woman wearing different crowns, costumes and ornaments.
